item: The release primitive sees a write round the ORM: a rows-changed baseline taken once per root transaction plus a before_cursor_execute non-read flag (statement_kind allowlist), the CHECK-3 lows of the R138 guard, and the hold policy on the three count-only re-index drains
summary: release_idle_connection declined only on what the ORM and its own flags recorded, so a write sent round the ORM, or a schema change or header PRAGMA that moves no row count, was rolled back without a sound by the release (the plain in_transaction flag cannot be used: SQLite reports it for a read pin, test_a_pinned_snapshot_is_released_at_the_boundary_so_the_log_can_be_checkpointed). It now compares the DBAPI connection's total_changes with a baseline taken once per ROOT transaction (after_begin also fires for a savepoint: retaking it there hid an unseen write, reproduced and pinned) and declines when an Engine before_cursor_execute listener flagged a statement that is not a plain read (an allowlist, an unknown statement is not a read; about 1.5 microseconds per statement on an engine that already had listeners, 5 on one that had none). reindex_all_batch, the corpus re-index job and the restore's re-index take the same should_flush hold policy as the backlog drain. the release, classifier, dead-connection, joined-connection and drain controls, 159 checks on the R138 guard; 13 + 19 + 9 + 16 mutants each killed by a named test; ruff total 413. Folded from the independent read: a connection the damage observer discarded is rolled back (the all-diagnostics build kept reading after a damaged member), a transaction with no connection is declined without checking one out, a Session joined to a connection with earlier writes sees them (the count is taken where the connection's own transaction begins), the re-index job's tally names the rule and the longest hold. Not seen, stated: DDL or a header PRAGMA sent straight to the DBAPI cursor.
